item.name: CLI log snapshot reader using shared redactor
item.contract: internal/cli/log_snapshot.go exposes type LogClass string with constants LogClassMain="main" and LogClassToolAudit="tool_audit", type LogSnapshotRoots struct{LogPath, ToolAuditPath string}, type SnapshotOpts struct{HeadBytes, TailBytes int64} (zero or negative HeadBytes/TailBytes default to 64*1024 and 16*1024 respectively), type LogSection struct{Class LogClass; Path string; Head, Tail []byte; Missing, Truncated bool; Redacted int; Unreadable string} and type Snapshot struct{Sections []LogSection}. SnapshotLogs(roots LogSnapshotRoots, opts SnapshotOpts) Snapshot returns Sections in order [LogClassMain, LogClassToolAudit] and ALWAYS includes both sections even when both files are absent. For each path: if os.Stat fails with os.IsNotExist, set Missing=true and skip read. If os.ReadFile fails for any other reason, set Unreadable to err.Error() and continue. If file size <= HeadBytes+TailBytes, set Head to the entire file content, Tail to nil, Truncated=false. If file size > HeadBytes+TailBytes, set Head to the first HeadBytes bytes, Tail to the last TailBytes bytes, Truncated=true. Then split each of Head and Tail by '\n' (bytes.Split), pass each non-empty line through RedactLine, sum the returned counts into LogSection.Redacted, and write the redacted lines back joined by '\n' into Head/Tail. The function never returns an error and never panics.

The command must reuse the existing setup/TUI toolset config machinery, persist `platform_toolsets.cli` without dropping unrelated config, print deterministic enabled/disabled/session-reset evidence, and keep gateway/channel `/tools` slash handling classified separately until a dedicated gateway row ports that surface.
item.degraded_mode: If the tool config cannot be loaded or a requested toolset/MCP server is unknown, the command returns bounded operator-facing evidence and must not call providers, mutate live sessions, or silently enable arbitrary tool names. Gateway/channel `/tools` remains unavailable until separately row-backed.
ready_when: The current root `gormes tools` command is still row-backed unavailable while TUI `/tools enable|disable` and setup tool config helpers already provide the narrow config machinery needed for CLI platform toggles.
The slice can be proven with hermetic config fixtures and does not require live providers, gateway sessions, MCP servers, or network access.
Existing untracked/draft runtime tests for `cmd/gormes/tools_command_test.go` can be adopted or rewritten by the builder, but planner must not edit runtime code.
not_ready_when: The builder broadens scope into gateway/channel `/tools`, model-visible tool registry changes, live session reset orchestration, setup wizard rewrites, or MCP server installation.
The implementation accepts arbitrary unknown tool names as enabled without evidence, drops unrelated config keys, or writes secrets to the repository.
The parity atom claims full `/tools` parity rather than partial root-CLI/TUI coverage with gateway slash still unavailable.
acceptance: `gormes tools list` reads the current CLI platform toolsets from a temp config fixture and prints tool names/status without `hermes_command_unavailable` or row-backed unavailable evidence.
`gormes tools enable web` persists `web` under `platform_toolsets.cli`, preserves existing entries and unrelated config, and prints deterministic `enabled: web` plus session-reset-required evidence.
`gormes tools disable terminal` removes only that CLI toolset, preserves remaining entries, and prints deterministic `disabled: terminal` plus session-reset-required evidence.
Parity docs classify `/tools` as partial with root CLI/TUI evidence and explicitly preserve the gateway/channel `/tools` gap.
item.note: Complete: TDD replaced the row-backed root `gormes tools` stubs with config-backed `tools list`, `tools enable <name...>`, and `tools disable <name...>` commands over existing CLI platform toolset config machinery. The command preserves existing selections, rejects unknown/MCP-missing names with evidence from the shared adapter, prints deterministic session-reset evidence, and leaves gateway/channel `/tools` parity explicitly separate.

item.name: Gormes-owned HTMX operator dashboard wiring
item.contract: `gormes dashboard` serves a working, navigable htmx/Templ operator web UI bound to loopback: the root and per-section page routes render full Templ documents, the previously empty `/dashboard` and `/api/logs` stub handlers are replaced, htmx fragment endpoints (`/ui/*`, `/dashboard/*`) return auto-escaped HTML partials for sessions, config, skills, cron, models, env, system, and logs, the Sessions/Config/Skills/Cron pages are repointed off non-existent JSON routes onto working fragments, four Gormes-owned parity pages (Env credential-presence, Models, System runtime stats, Logs) plus nav links are added, user-supplied task-injection input is HTML-escaped, fragment data is loopback-open but requires dashboard auth when network-exposed, and the command feeds live env-key presence, config-path, and installed-skill data through typed seams without leaking secret values. This is a Gormes-owned presentation surface (htmx in Go) that intentionally diverges from Hermes' React/Vite dashboard; behavioral/data parity is the gate, not visual parity. Dashboard chat is backed by the native kernel turn loop: the `gormes dashboard` command builds a provider client + default tool registry + kernel through a CLI-layer factory seam (avoiding an app->cli import cycle) and injects it as the apiserver turn loop, the chat task-injection endpoint runs a real streaming turn and broadcasts escaped tokens / final reply / errors to the SSE feed, and a missing provider degrades chat to display-only instead of failing dashboard startup. Dashboard chat is persisted: the kernel uses the shared SQLite transcript store (memory.db) so chats appear in `gormes session list` and survive restart, and the dashboard session id is mapped in the bbolt session map (sessions.db) best-effort (skipped when the gateway holds the exclusive lock) so transcript persistence never depends on it. A 'new chat' control resets the agent conversation (clearing kernel context via the turn loop's ResetSession seam when wired) and rotates the dashboard chat session id so the next conversation persists as its own session record, clearing the visible feed. The dashboard command also feeds live Cron and Sessions data: the Sessions page reads the persistent session directory (memory.db, the same source as `gormes session list`) and the Cron page reads the real cron store (bbolt session DB); both degrade gracefully when their store is unavailable, and the chat turn loop no longer opens the bbolt session map so sessions.db is free for the cron store. Dashboard chat reloads on restart: the turn-loop factory replays the persisted dashboard-chat transcript into the kernel via ResumeSession so the agent remembers prior context, and the chat feed loads the persisted transcript on page load via a ChatHistory seam so the operator sees the prior conversation.
item.degraded_mode: Unwired data sources (turn loop, cron store, config summary, skills, env) render a graceful 'not wired' / empty-state notice instead of 500ing; a network-exposed dashboard returns 401 on fragment data without auth; the JSON /api/* and /v1/* programmatic surface keeps its existing bearer-key gate unchanged.
ready_when: The apiserver Templ pages, layout, embedded htmx asset, JSON dashboard endpoints, and SSE hub already exist but page/fragment routes were never registered and `/dashboard` was an empty stub.
Templ can be regenerated with `go run github.com/a-h/templ/cmd/templ@v0.3.1001 generate`.
Live env-key presence, config paths, and installed-skill listing are readable without network or provider auth.
not_ready_when: The slice ports Hermes' React/Vite runtime, plugin JS execution, or the in-browser PTY chat pane.
Fragment endpoints surface secret credential values instead of presence-only status.

item.note: 2026-06-16 Gormes-owned dashboard slice. The apiserver already had a strong JSON/SSE surface and orphaned Templ pages, but the HTML dashboard was unwired (`/dashboard` and `/api/logs` were empty stubs, nav routes 404'd, Config/Skills pages pointed at non-existent /api/config and /api/skills). This slice wires page + fragment routes, replaces the stubs, adds Env/Models/System/Logs parity pages, fixes task-injection XSS, makes logs.Store a real bounded ring buffer, and feeds live env/config/skills data through typed seams in the dashboard command. Verified live: every page and fragment returns 200 and unknown paths 404. Follow-up (2026-06-16): wired the native kernel turn loop into dashboard chat via a CLI-layer BuildTurnLoop factory seam; chat now runs real streaming agent turns with graceful display-only degradation when no provider is configured. Verified live: configured endpoint -> turn executes and streams to SSE; unconfigured -> display-only. Follow-up (2026-06-16): persisted dashboard chat to the shared SQLite transcript store (memory.db) under the stable 'dashboard-chat' session and mapped the session id in sessions.db (bbolt, best-effort under gateway lock). Verified live: a chat turn writes a user turn row to memory.db and the session appears in `gormes session list`. Follow-up (2026-06-16): added a 'new chat' reset button — POST /agent/reset calls KernelTurnLoop.ResetSession (clears kernel history) and rotates the chat session id so the next chat persists separately. Verified live: reset then chat yields two distinct session ids in memory.db. Follow-up (2026-06-16): fixed SSE so the browser actually renders streamed frames — bundled the htmx-ext-sse extension (was missing; only htmx core loaded) and made broadcastSSE emit named `event: frame` frames (was unnamed data, so sse-swap='frame' never matched). Verified in Chromium: the chat feed now shows the SSE-delivered user echo and turn result, not just the POST ack. Follow-up (2026-06-16): wired the live nav status indicator — each SSE connection emits an initial + 5s-ticked named 'status' frame, and the (previously duplicated, unconnected) #nav-status div now has sse-connect/sse-swap='status'. Verified in Chromium: nav shows '● live <model>' instead of 'Connecting…'. Follow-up (2026-06-17): wired live Cron and Sessions data into the dashboard command. Sessions page reads the persistent session directory (memory.db) via a SessionsList seam; Cron page reads the real cron store via cronapp.OpenStore. Removed the now-redundant bbolt session-map open from the chat turn-loop factory so sessions.db is free for the cron store (apiserver owns the chat session id). Verified live: /ui/cron shows the wired empty store ('No cron jobs.') and /ui/sessions shows a real persisted session after a chat. Follow-up (2026-06-17): polished real token-by-token streaming render — each token delta is its own SSE frame appended after a 🤖 assistant marker, with a line terminator at end and a larger SSE client buffer (256) so bursty deltas are not dropped. Verified live against a fake streaming provider in Chromium: the reply filled in token-by-token (captured mid-stream partial then complete). Follow-up (2026-06-17): added chat history reload on restart. The factory loads the dashboard-chat transcript (transcript.LoadMessages on memory.db) and calls kernel.ResumeSession so the agent remembers across restarts; the chat feed loads /dashboard/chat-history on page load via a ChatHistory seam (sourced from the same transcript). Verified live: after a restart the resume log reports 'resumed prior chat history messages=2' and the browser feed shows the prior user+assistant conversation.
done_signal: Dashboard pages and htmx fragments render live data with graceful degradation, task-injection input is escaped, network-exposed fragments require auth, and the full Go test suite plus progress validate stay green.
